page: Vultr vbm-8c-132gb is a dedicated bare-metal server belonging to the Bare Metal NVMe family. It is equipped with a single Intel Xeon E-2288G processor operating at a base frequency of 3.7 GHz across 8 physical cores and 16 execution threads on the x86_64 architecture. Hardware features include 16 MB of L3 cache, support for AVX, AES-NI, and hardware virtualization via VMX. The configuration includes 128 GB of DDR4 memory clocked at 3 GHz, providing an allocation of 8 GB per logical thread. Fast local persistence is supplied by a bundled 3840 GB NVMe solid-state drive, accompanied by one complimentary public IPv4 address. The server features no dedicated GPU hardware.

Benchmark evaluations position the platform well for memory-intensive workloads and single-threaded operations. The system scored 3594.89 on the PassMark memory suite, landing in the top decile of measured systems, complemented by strong throughput in single-threaded gzip compression at 36.22 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 14.23 GB/sec. General multi-core processing registers in the middle tier, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 8690.0 and a multi-threaded stress-ng result of 19837.37. Uncached large-block memory bandwidth demonstrated lower efficiency, recording 29.76 GB/sec read and 15.32 GB/sec write speeds in the bottom quartile.

Without hypervisor overhead or shared tenancy, this bare-metal profile provides predictable I/O and computing consistency. The substantial 3.84 TB NVMe disk array paired with 128 GB of RAM suits memory-heavy caching engines, high-capacity relational databases, intermediate ETL pipelines, and high-concurrency static web serving. Conversely, the absence of vector acceleration beyond standard AVX and the lack of discrete GPUs make it ill-suited for larger artificial intelligence model inference.
description: Vultr vbm-8c-132gb is a bare-metal server powered by an 8-core, 16-thread Intel Xeon E-2288G processor running at 3.7 GHz on x86_64 architecture. The hardware configuration features 128 GB of DDR4 system memory alongside 3840 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage, offering an 8:1 memory-to-thread ratio without virtualization overhead. Benchmark results reveal strong single-threaded data compression alongside a top-tier PassMark memory score of 3594.89, while multi-core compute metrics such as Geekbench and stress-ng remain in the median range. Due to its dedicated CPU resources, dense memory capacity, and integrated NVMe storage, this server functions effectively for intermediate database systems, Redis in-memory caches, software compilation, and dedicated web application hosting that require consistent disk I/O and dedicated CPU execution.
